sources: Feld (1991), Why your friends have more friends than you do, American Journal of Sociology 96(6), 1464–1477 – the 'friendship paradox': popular people appear in many friend lists, so the mean number of friends of friends exceeds the mean number of friends; in Coleman's Marketville high-school data 80 of 146 girls (55%) had fewer friends than the mean of their friends, 41 had more, 25 the same; mean 2.7 friends vs 3.4 for friends.
